title: WCL Asst. Foreman (Electrical) — Mock 05
pattern: WCL Asst. Foreman (Electrical) CBT (100 Q · 100 marks · 120 min · no −ve)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: When workings approach within 60 m of a water body or waterlogged area, the manager shall:
options: Stop working immediately without any plan
Leave the water body untouched forever
Only mark it on the board
Prepare a scheme for protection against inrush and drain the water in a planned manner
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 149 (danger from surface water) & Ch. XI: within 60 m, protective schemes (drainage, barriers) are implemented.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: In gassy mines, electric lighting from a source external to the lighting unit may be used on any roadway or place:
options: Ventilated by intake air or not within 270 m of the nearest face
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 176(1): external-source electric lighting is permitted on intake-air roadways or places not within 270 m of the nearest face.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: In return airways and old workings, the air shall normally contain oxygen not less than ______ and carbon dioxide not more than ______.
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 165: not less than 19% oxygen and not more than 0.5% carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The maximum torque of a synchronous motor occurs at torque angle:
questions.solution: Maximum torque (pull-out torque) occurs at δ = 90°.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: If the load on a synchronous motor exceeds pull-out torque:
questions.solution: Motor pulls out of synchronism and stalls.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Every engine, motor, transformer and battery-charging room on the surface of a mine shall be provided with at least:
options: Two exits, properly maintained and kept free from obstruction
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 212: such rooms are kept clean and provided with at least two exits, properly maintained and free from obstruction.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A synchronous motor operating at leading power factor is equivalent to:
questions.solution: Leading power factor means it supplies reactive power, like a capacitor.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The power consumed by a synchronous motor is proportional to:
questions.solution: P = (3V Eb / Xs) × sin δ, but torque ∝ sin δ, and power ∝ torque × speed (constant).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: For electrical machinery and plant, the competent person for inspection under CMR 2017 shall be an engineer or electrician holding qualifications specified in:
options: CEA (Measures relating to Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations, 2010
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 213(6): the competent person for electrical machinery holds qualifications as specified in the CEA Safety & Electric Supply Regulations, 2010.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A servo motor is characterized by:
questions.solution: Servo motors are designed for fast response, precise control of position/speed/torque.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A stepper motor converts:
options: Electrical pulses to discrete mechanical steps
questions.solution: Stepper motor moves in fixed angular steps in response to electrical pulses.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The step angle of a stepper motor is determined by:
options: Number of stator phases and rotor teeth
questions.solution: Step angle = 360° / (number of phases × number of rotor teeth × gear ratio).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A BLDC (Brushless DC) motor differs from a DC motor in that:
questions.solution: BLDC uses electronic commutation (Hall sensors + MOSFETs/IGBTs) instead of brushes.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A universal motor can operate on:
questions.solution: Universal motor is a series-wound motor designed to run on both AC and DC supply.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A repulsion motor works on the principle of:
options: Repulsion between stator field and rotor poles
questions.solution: Repulsion between stator magnetic field and induced rotor poles produces torque.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The speed of a universal motor on no load tends to:
questions.solution: Like a series DC motor, universal motor speed rises dangerously high at no load.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A hysteresis motor works on the principle of:
options: Hysteresis and eddy current losses in rotor
questions.solution: Hysteresis motor uses hysteresis loss in special rotor material to produce torque.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A reluctance motor runs at:
questions.solution: Reluctance motor runs at synchronous speed due to reluctance torque.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A shaded pole motor is used in:
questions.solution: Shaded pole motor is cheap, low torque, used in fans, blowers, small appliances.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The starting torque of a shaded pole motor is:
questions.solution: Starting torque is low due to weak rotating field from shading coil.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) uses:
questions.solution: PMSM uses permanent magnets (rare earth) on rotor for excitation.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The main advantage of PMSM over induction motor is:
questions.solution: PMSM has no rotor copper loss, giving higher efficiency.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The hunting in a synchronous motor can be reduced by:
questions.solution: Damper windings damp oscillations by producing opposing torque during hunting.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A synchronous motor can be used for power factor correction by:
questions.solution: Over-excited synchronous motor draws leading current, acting as a synchronous condenser.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The field winding of a synchronous motor is supplied by:
options: DC supply (via slip rings or brushless exciter)
questions.solution: Rotor field winding is excited by DC through slip rings or brushless exciter.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The starting current of a synchronous motor is typically:
questions.solution: Synchronous motor draws 5–7× rated current at DOL start.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A brushless DC motor uses which type of rotor?
questions.solution: BLDC uses permanent magnet rotor with electronic commutation.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The torque in a stepper motor is proportional to:
questions.solution: Torque is proportional to stator current (up to magnetic saturation).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: If the percentage of inflammable gas in the general body of air exceeds ______, persons shall be withdrawn from the working.
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 166: persons are withdrawn when the general body of air exceeds 1.25% inflammable gas.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A servo system typically uses which feedback device?
questions.solution: Encoders or resolvers provide position/speed feedback for closed-loop servo control.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The rotor of a hysteresis motor is made of:
questions.solution: Hard magnetic material with high hysteresis loss is used for the rotor.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A single-phase induction motor is not self-starting because:
questions.solution: Single-phase produces pulsating (not rotating) field, so no starting torque.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a starting method of a single-phase induction motor?
questions.solution: Capacitor start, shaded pole, and split-phase (resistance start) are standard single-phase induction motor starting methods; autotransformer starting is used for three-phase motors.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A capacitor-start capacitor-run motor uses:
options: One capacitor for starting, removed after start
Two capacitors (one for start, one for run)
questions.solution: Starting capacitor (large) is disconnected by centrifugal switch; run capacitor stays.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The direction of rotation of a single-phase motor can be reversed by:
questions.solution: Reversing either main or starting winding connections reverses rotating field direction.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Approaching a goaf, probing shall be carried out ahead of the working for at least:
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 147: the working is probed ahead for at least 1.5 m beyond the last support before approaching the goaf.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The synchronous speed of an 8-pole motor at 50 Hz is:

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: While driving approaching old or waterlogged workings, advance boreholes shall be kept at least ______ ahead of the face.
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 163: at least 3 advance boreholes not less than 3 m ahead of the face, with flank holes within 5 m on either side.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The pull-out torque of a synchronous motor is typically:
questions.solution: Pull-out torque is typically 1.5–2 times rated torque.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A brushless DC motor is basically a:
options: Permanent magnet synchronous motor with electronic commutation
questions.solution: BLDC is a PMSM with electronic commutation (trapezoidal back-EMF).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The speed of a stepper motor is controlled by:
questions.solution: Stepper motor speed is directly proportional to pulse frequency.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A synchronous motor can be started as an induction motor using:
questions.solution: Damper windings act as squirrel cage rotor for induction motor starting.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The efficiency of a synchronous motor is generally:
questions.solution: Synchronous motor has no rotor copper loss (DC excited), giving higher efficiency.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A permanent magnet stepper motor has step angle of 1.8°. How many steps per revolution?
questions.solution: Steps per revolution = 360° / 1.8° = 200 steps.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) controls motor speed by:
questions.solution: V/f control maintains constant flux for optimal motor performance.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) in a VFD is used to:
options: Control voltage amplitude by varying pulse width
questions.solution: PWM varies pulse width to control effective voltage amplitude.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The DC bus in a VFD converts:
options: Both AC to DC and DC to AC
questions.solution: VFD: Rectifier (AC→DC) → DC Bus → Inverter (DC→AC with V/f control).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A soft starter reduces motor starting current by:
questions.solution: Soft starter uses back-to-back thyristors to ramp voltage from low to full.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The main advantage of a VFD over a soft starter is:
questions.solution: VFD provides continuous speed control; soft starter only reduces starting current.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) uses which programming language for basic logic?
questions.solution: Ladder logic is the most common PLC programming language, mimicking relay logic.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The input module of a PLC receives signals from:
options: Sensors (push buttons, limit switches, proximity sensors)
questions.solution: Input modules receive field signals from sensors and switches.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The output module of a PLC sends signals to:
questions.solution: Output modules drive actuators based on program logic.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: SCADA stands for:
questions.solution: SCADA provides supervisory monitoring and control of industrial processes.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: DCS stands for:
questions.solution: DCS distributes control functions across multiple controllers for process plants.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The difference between SCADA and DCS is:
options: SCADA is for monitoring, DCS for control
SCADA is for DC, DCS for AC
SCADA is for large distributed systems, DCS for continuous processes
questions.solution: SCADA monitors distributed sites; DCS controls continuous processes locally.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An AC drive (VFD) for an induction motor typically includes:
questions.solution: AC drive: Rectifier (AC→DC) → DC bus capacitor → Inverter (DC→AC).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A DC drive controls DC motor speed by:
options: Varying armature voltage and field current
questions.solution: DC drive varies armature voltage (below base speed) and field current (above base speed).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: In a gassy seam of the second or third degree, no person shall supervise or operate electrical machinery unless he:
options: Holds a gas-testing certificate and carries an approved flame safety lamp
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 213(2): in 2nd/3rd-degree gassy seams, operators of electrical machinery (other than telephones/signals/lamps) hold a gas-testing certificate and carry an approved flame safety lamp.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The dynamic braking in a VFD dissipates energy in:
questions.solution: DC bus energy is dissipated as heat in an external braking resistor via a chopper.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The slip power recovery drive is used with:
questions.solution: Slip power recovery captures rotor slip energy and feeds it back to supply.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The Kramer drive is a type of:
questions.solution: Kramer drive converts slip power to mechanical power and feeds it back to shaft.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The Scherbius drive is a type of:
questions.solution: Scherbius drive converts slip power to electrical power and feeds it back to supply.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The energy savings from using a VFD on a centrifugal pump/fan application follows:
questions.solution: For centrifugal loads: Power ∝ N³, so small speed reduction gives large power savings.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: If a fan speed is reduced from 100% to 80% using VFD, power consumption reduces to approximately:
questions.solution: Power ∝ N³, so (0.8)³ = 0.512 = ~51% of full load power.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The V/f ratio of a VFD is kept constant to:
questions.solution: Constant V/f maintains constant air gap flux, preventing saturation at low frequency.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: At very low frequencies (below 5 Hz), VFD applies:
options: Voltage boost to overcome stator IR drop
questions.solution: Voltage boost compensates for stator resistance voltage drop at low frequencies.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Every mechanised outlet (shaft or incline) is examined at least once in every 7 days by:
options: An engineer, electrical supervisor or foreman, or a competent person authorised by the engineer
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 75(2): mechanised outlets are examined at least once in 7 days by an engineer, electrical supervisor or foreman (or authorised competent person), recorded in a bound paged book.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Under CMR 2017, a thorough inspection of all machinery and plant in use is required at least once in every:
options: 7 days, recorded in a bound paged book
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 213(5): a competent person thoroughly inspects all machinery and plant at least once in 7 days, recording results in a bound paged book.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Under the Mines Act 1952, an Inspector may, among other powers:
options: Enter, inspect and examine a mine, and make inquiries on any matter relating to safety
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.22: Inspectors may enter, inspect, examine and inquire into any mine and its records.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Direct Torque Control (DTC) in a VFD controls:
options: Torque and flux directly using motor model
questions.solution: DTC estimates torque and flux from motor model and directly controls them.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The braking chopper in a VFD is used for:
questions.solution: Chopper switches braking resistor across DC bus for dynamic braking.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An active front end (AFE) in a VFD enables:
questions.solution: AFE uses controlled rectifier (IGBT-based) for bidirectional power flow.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The harmonic distortion caused by a VFD can be reduced by:
options: Adding line reactor or input filter
questions.solution: Line reactors and filters reduce harmonics drawn from supply by the rectifier.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A 12-pulse rectifier in a VFD is used to:
questions.solution: 12-pulse rectifier reduces 5th and 7th harmonics compared to 6-pulse.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The communication protocol commonly used between VFD and PLC is:
questions.solution: Modbus RTU/TCP is the most common industrial communication protocol for VFDs.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A PLC scan cycle consists of:
options: Input scan, program execution, output scan, housekeeping
questions.solution: PLC scan: Read inputs → Execute program → Update outputs → Diagnostics.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The memory of a PLC where input/output status is stored is called:
questions.solution: Input/output image table stores the status of all I/O points during scan.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A PLC timer function used for delay-on is called:
questions.solution: TON generates output after input is true for preset time.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A PLC counter function that counts rising edges is:
questions.solution: CTU counts rising edges of input signal.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The HMI (Human Machine Interface) in an industrial system is used for:
questions.solution: HMI provides graphical display of process status and allows operator commands.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Synonym of EVANESCENT:
questions.solution: Evanescent: quickly fading, fleeting

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Antonym of TRANSPARENT:
questions.solution: Transparent: clear; antonym: opaque

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Idiom 'Piece of cake' means:
questions.solution: Piece of cake: very easy

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Idiom 'To break the ice' means:
questions.solution: Break the ice: initiate social interaction

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Idiom 'A bolt from the blue' means:
questions.solution: Bolt from blue: completely unexpected

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Fill in blank: She has been absent ___ Monday.
questions.solution: Since + point of time

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Fill in blank: He is senior ___ me.
questions.solution: Senior to (not senior than)

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Fill in blank: Neither he ___ I am going.
questions.solution: Neither...nor (correlative conjunction)

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Correct spelling:
questions.solution: Accommodation (double c, double m)

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Identify error: He don't know the answer.
questions.solution: 'He' takes 'doesn't' (third person singular)

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Synonym of CAPRICIOUS:
questions.solution: Capricious: unpredictable, fickle

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Synonym of PERSEVERE:
questions.solution: Persevere = persist, continue

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Antonym of COURAGEOUS:
questions.solution: Courageous: brave; antonym: cowardly

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Voice change: She sings a song. (Passive)
options: A song was sung by her
A song has been sung by her
A song is sung by her
questions.solution: Present simple passive: is/are + V3

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Fill in blank: He goes to school ___ foot.
questions.solution: On foot (idiomatic)

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: A can do work in 10 days, B in 15 days. Together in:
questions.solution: 1/10+1/15=1/6; together 6 days
